title: Five new guides to choosing and living with vintage furniture
description: Visible joints, several lamps in one room, an old picture frame, second-hand curtains, and furnishing a rental you will move out of. Published in English, Dutch and German.
label: New Guides

sections.heading: Five new guides
paragraphs: Most PatinaHall guides answer a question you ask in front of a listing. These five are asked slightly later — once the piece is yours, or once you are standing in a flat you do not own. All five are published in English, Dutch and German, and are in the Guides hub under their topics.

What a visible furniture joint can tell you — keeps three things apart that are easy to confuse: how a piece was built, what condition it is in, and whether it can be taken apart to get up the stairs.
Several vintage lamps, one comfortable room — gives each old lamp a job rather than a position, and builds an evening plan around the people using the room.
An old frame for a picture you already love — measures the visible opening, the rebate behind it and the usable depth before anyone promises the picture will fit.
Vintage curtains that fit your window — compares a second-hand pair against your own track or pole: finished width, drop, heading, lining, and what an alteration can realistically rescue.
Vintage furniture for this rental and the next move — choosing pieces you can live with now while recording how they came in, what the largest single part is, and what moving them again will involve.

sections.heading: Fifteen existing guides went deeper
paragraphs: The same release expanded fifteen guides that were already published — among them measuring a table for a room, measuring furniture for the route into your home, measuring a vintage bed for a modern mattress, telling teak from walnut and rosewood, reading solid wood against veneer and laminate, judging restored or refinished pieces, and arranging professional delivery.
